knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is used to treat streptococcal meningitis.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Fleming first used the purified penicillin to treat streptococcal meningitis in 1942.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is used to treat neonatal conjunctivitis.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Cecil George Paine was the first to successfully use penicillin to treat eye infection (neonatal conjunctivitis) in 1930.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is licensed for the treatment of anthrax.
knowledge_cards.source_span: It is also licensed for the treatment of anthrax

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is used as an adjunctive therapy to treat tetanus.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is licensed to treat syphilis.
knowledge_cards.source_span: meningococcal meningitis and/or septicaemia caused by penicillin-susceptible organisms and syphilis.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin kills bacteria by inhibiting the completion of the synthesis of peptidoglycans.
knowledge_cards.answer: inhibiting the completion of the synthesis of peptidoglycans
knowledge_cards.source_span: Penicillin kills bacteria by inhibiting the completion of the synthesis of peptidoglycans, the structural component of the bacterial cell wall.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin acts by binding to penicillin binding proteins.
knowledge_cards.source_span: It does this by binding to penicillin binding proteins with the β-lactam ring, a structure found on penicillin molecules.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin specifically inhibits the activity of enzymes needed for the cross-linking of peptidoglycans.
knowledge_cards.source_span: It specifically inhibits the activity of enzymes that are needed for the cross-linking of peptidoglycans during the final step in cell wall biosynthesis.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin inactivates DD-transpeptidase.
knowledge_cards.source_span: As a consequence, DD-transpeptidase is inactivated, the formation of cross-links between UDP-MurNAc and N-acetyl glucosamine is blocked

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin causes cell lysis and death in bacteria.
knowledge_cards.source_span: This results in cell lysis and death.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: A common adverse drug reaction associated with the use of penicillins is diarrhoea.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Nausea is a common side effect of penicillin.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Neurotoxicity is a common adverse effect associated with penicillin.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin can induce serum sickness in some individuals.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Penicillin can also induce serum sickness or a serum sickness-like reaction in some individuals.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Pseudomembranous colitis is an infrequent adverse effect of penicillin.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Infrequent adverse effects (0.1–1% of people) include fever, vomiting, erythema, dermatitis, angioedema, seizures (especially in people with epilepsy), and pseudomembranous colitis.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Penicillin is originally obtained from Penicillium rubens.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin deficiency is associated with type 1 diabetes.
knowledge_cards.source_span: In type 1 diabetes, the beta cells are destroyed by an autoimmune reaction so that insulin can no longer be synthesized or be secreted into the blood.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Decreased or absent insulin activity results in hyperglycaemia.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Decreased or absent insulin activity results in diabetes, a condition of high blood sugar level (hyperglycaemia).

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin promotes the absorption of glucose from the blood into cells.
knowledge_cards.source_span: promoting the absorption of glucose from the blood into cells of the liver, fat, and skeletal muscles.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin inhibits gluconeogenesis in the liver.
knowledge_cards.source_span: glucose production by the liver through glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis are inhibited.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin operates via the activation of phosphoinositol 3 kinase.
knowledge_cards.source_span: operates via the activation, by IRS-1, of phosphoinositol 3 kinase (PI3K).

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin decreases lipolysis in fat cells.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Decreased lipolysis in – forces reduction in conversion of fat cell lipid stores into blood fatty acids and glycerol

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The most common cause of hypoglycemia is medications used to treat diabetes such as insulin.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin can result in seizures.
knowledge_cards.source_span: This may result in a variety of symptoms including clumsiness, trouble talking, confusion, loss of consciousness, seizures or death.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Insulin aggregation can cause injection amyloidosis.
knowledge_cards.source_span: This can cause injection amyloidosis, and prevents the storage of insulin for long periods.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sweating is a symptom of low blood sugar caused by insulin.
knowledge_cards.source_span: A feeling of hunger, sweating, shakiness and weakness may also be present.
